title: Rectangular detection of a continuous homogeneous cocycle
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a topology for which addition, negation and multiplication $K\times K\to K$ are continuous, and let $G$ be a group with a topology for which multiplication and inversion are continuous. Let $M$ be a topological $K$-vector space with continuous $K$-linear left $G$-action (addition, negation, scalar multiplication and the action are continuous). Let $n\geq1$, let $H\subseteq G$ be an open subgroup with its induced topology [def-kun-subspace-topology], and choose $a_0,\ldots,a_n\in G$. Suppose $f:G^{n+1}\to M$ is continuous, is diagonally equivariant, $f(gg_0,\ldots,gg_n)=g f(g_0,\ldots,g_n)$, and is a homogeneous cocycle, meaning $\delta f=0$ for the differential $(\delta f)(g_0,\ldots,g_{n+1})=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^i f(g_0,\ldots,\widehat{g_i},\ldots,g_{n+1})$. If $f(h_0a_0,\ldots,h_na_n)=0$ for every $(h_0,\ldots,h_n)\in H^{n+1}$, then there is a continuous diagonally $H$-equivariant $t:H^n\to M$ with $f|_{H^{n+1}}=\delta t$, where $(\delta t)(h_0,\ldots,h_n)=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^i t(h_0,\ldots,\widehat{h_i},\ldots,h_n)$. The assertion concerns actual continuous cochains; no closure of the coboundaries or completeness of $M$ is imposed.

proof.text: Let $B_q(Y)$ be the integral tuple chains with augmentation $d[y]=1$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. The alternating boundary has $d^2=0$: deleting original positions $i<j$ in opposite orders gives signs $(-1)^{i+j-1}$ and $(-1)^{i+j}$. Extend $f$ additively to $F:B_n(G)\to M$. The cocycle equation is $Fd=0$ on $B_{n+1}(G)$, and diagonal equivariance gives $F(gz)=gF(z)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ordered-join-coset-comparison] to $G,H,n,(a_i)$ and set $A=eP$. This gives an $H$-equivariant augmented chain map through degree $n$, equal to $1$ in degree $-1$, with a fixed finite coordinate formula using $h_ja_i$. Its degree-$n$ image is spanned by the ordered rectangle tuples, on each of which $F$ vanishes by hypothesis. Thus $FA_n=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent arithmetic expansion; assembly step 2; original argument retained in the extracted comparison and prefix-homotopy nodes and the worker report.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-homogeneous-tuple-prefix-homotopy] to this $A$ and inclusion $I:B(H)\to B(G)$. All its hypotheses are supplied by the preceding step. Obtain $H$-equivariant $Q_q$ through degree $n$ with $I_q-A_q=dQ_q+Q_{q-1}d$. Each $Q_q$ has a fixed finite integer formula in tuples with coordinates $h_j$ or $h_ja_i$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent arithmetic expansion; assembly step 3; original argument retained in the extracted comparison and prefix-homotopy nodes and the worker report.

proof.text: Define $t(h_0,\ldots,h_{n-1})=FQ_{n-1}[h_0,\ldots,h_{n-1}]$, using $n\geq1$. The finite formula supplied by [lem-sfb-homogeneous-tuple-prefix-homotopy] writes $t$ as a fixed finite integer sum of evaluations of $f$. Each substituted coordinate is a projection followed by $H\hookrightarrow G$, continuous by [def-kun-subspace-topology], optionally followed by right multiplication by a fixed $a_i$, continuous by multiplication in $G$. The tuple maps and their composites with $f$ are therefore continuous; finite sums and negations in $M$ preserve continuity. Equivariance of $F,Q$ gives $t(gh_0,\ldots,gh_{n-1})=g\,t(h_0,\ldots,h_{n-1})$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent arithmetic expansion; assembly step 4; original argument retained in the extracted comparison and prefix-homotopy nodes and the worker report.

proof.text: Apply $F$ to the degree-$n$ identity from [lem-sfb-homogeneous-tuple-prefix-homotopy]: $FI_n-FA_n=FdQ_n+FQ_{n-1}d$. Since $FA_n=0$ and $Fd=0$, this is $f(h_0,\ldots,h_n)=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^i t(h_0,\ldots,\widehat{h_i},\ldots,h_n)$. This equality uses only finite integer sums in the actual coefficient group, in every characteristic, without a closure or completeness assumption.
